text: The authors call the active learning setting the most interesting, where the agent requests reward on the most useful episodes or timesteps and must economise on both feedback requests and training time; a random setting, with reward visible on a random subset, is also considered. The baseline ignores unlabeled episodes and runs ordinary RL on labeled ones, which generally learns slowly; the challenge is to use unlabeled episodes to learn almost as quickly and robustly as with all episodes labeled.
title: Active vs random reward visibility in semi-supervised RL, and the naive baseline
